text: Weed management (ការគ្រប់គ្រងស្មៅ) should focus on preventing weeds from competing strongly with the crop during its most vulnerable growth stages, not on keeping every field completely weed-free all season. This matters most in the wet season (រដូវវស្សា), when warm, frequent rainfall encourages rapid weed emergence; irrigated vegetable plots can still develop substantial weed pressure in the dry season (រដូវប្រាំង). In rain-fed fields, avoid unnecessary cultivation after rainfall, since repeated disturbance increases labor and can bring new weed seeds to the surface. Practical smallholder methods: hand weeding (ការដកស្មៅ), hoeing/simple mechanical cultivation, appropriate crop density, timely planting, mulching, and keeping field edges and irrigation channels from becoming weed sources. For rice, weed pressure depends on whether the farmer uses direct seeding (សាបព្រោះ, where crop and weed seedlings emerge together and compete hard) or transplanting (ស្ទូង, where transplanted seedlings have a size advantage). For cassava, early weed control matters most since the crop grows slowly before forming a full canopy. Cashew orchards need attention to weeds around young trees, but excessive bare-soil cultivation increases erosion, especially on sloped land in the wet season. Vegetables often need frequent early control due to close spacing and shallow roots. Herbicides should NOT be the default recommendation -- if used, the product must be legally appropriate for the crop and weed and follow the current Cambodian label and safety requirements; do not name a herbicide product or give an application rate without verifying current Cambodian registration. For species-specific advice, ask the farmer what crop they're growing and what the weed looks like (or request a photo) rather than assuming a 'common Preah Vihear weed' without district-level evidence.
